target_customer: Commercial real estate developers and property owners installing EV chargers
problem: Installing EV chargers at commercial properties involves buying hardware, hiring installers and applying for government incentives. Overflux aimed to automate all three.
business_model: Service fee or margin on EV charger purchase and installation plus incentive application

founders.name: Richard Zhang
founders.background_notes: From YC page bio: product at Alibaba Cloud, data science at DiDi, investing at Dragonfly and Gaorong Capital. Education not listed.

founders.name: Ari Sokolov
founders.background_notes: No bio on the YC page.

competitors.name: Qmerit
competitors.what: Installer network offering turnkey EV charging for commercial properties including assessment, scope and installation
competitors.traction_then: Launched its commercial turnkey offering in 2022

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly workflow software and coordination of installers and incentive paperwork, with no novel hardware or algorithms.

defensibility.rationale: Service layer that established installers such as Qmerit and charger vendors could replicate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent installers and charger vendors already sold turnkey commercial offerings; no source records what they did about Overflux.

market_need_then: Federal and state incentives and rising EV adoption in 2022 created demand for commercial charger installs, and incentive amounts of thousands of dollars per charger made paperwork valuable to developers.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community material about the brand was found; searches returned only the YC page.

outcome_analysis: Overflux was a two person YC W23 company automating commercial EV charger purchase, installation and incentive filing. The only public status signal is the Inactive label on its YC page. No shutdown post, press coverage or funding news exists, so the cause of failure is not public and no failure factors are asserted.
